findings.detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner (self-hosted) of a private or internal repository that runs the workflows of pull requests from its forks
findings.consequence: one who may read the repository and fork it, which every member of the enterprise reads for an internal one, can open a pull request that runs their code on the runner, whose state persists for the jobs after it: their secrets, their tokens and the runner's network
findings.remedy: turn off Run workflows from fork pull requests, which the rule reads as the fact repo.fork-pr-run-workflows (with the fact false, the rule reports nothing), or run the jobs on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. On self-hosted runners that no pull request from a fork reaches, declare a label of runs-on that only those runners have trusted with the fact repo.runner-label-trusted (true for the label, in a file of facts, --fact, or fact in --config): the rule then reports nothing for the job. An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.

findings.detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner (self-hosted) of a public repository
findings.consequence: anyone who opens a pull request can run their code on the runner, whose state persists for the jobs after it: their secrets, their tokens and the runner's network
findings.remedy: run the jobs of a public repository on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. An owner of the organization can instead put the self-hosted runners in a runner group that does not allow public repositories: no job of the repository reaches those runners; declare a label of runs-on that only those runners have trusted with the fact repo.runner-label-trusted (true for the label, in a file of facts, --fact, or fact in --config), and the rule reports nothing for the job (otherwise the false positive form group-access). An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.

findings.detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner (self-hosted) of a public repository
findings.consequence: anyone who opens a pull request can run their code on the runner, whose state persists for the jobs after it: their secrets, their tokens and the runner's network
findings.remedy: run the jobs of a public repository on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. An owner of the organization can instead put the self-hosted runners in a runner group that does not allow public repositories: no job of the repository reaches those runners; declare a label of runs-on that only those runners have trusted with the fact repo.runner-label-trusted (true for the label, in a file of facts, --fact, or fact in --config), and the rule reports nothing for the job (otherwise the false positive form group-access). An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.

findings.detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner (self-hosted) of a private or internal repository that runs the workflows of pull requests from its forks

findings.remedy: turn off Run workflows from fork pull requests, which the rule reads as the fact repo.fork-pr-run-workflows (with the fact false, the rule reports nothing), or run the jobs on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. On self-hosted runners that no pull request from a fork reaches, declare a label of runs-on that only those runners have trusted with the fact repo.runner-label-trusted (true for the label, in a file of facts, --fact, or fact in --config): the rule then reports nothing for the job. An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.

findings.remedy: A variable of env and double quotes ("$X") stop the shell from running the value as code, but the variable and the quotes do not stop the command from reading the value as an option. In either fix below, keep the value in the variable of env, and pass the variable to the command inside double quotes. Then either put the word that ends the command's options (--; --end-of-options for git) after the last option the command needs and before the value, for example right before the value (tar -xf archive.tar notes.txt -- "$X"), so that the command reads every word after that word as a plain argument; or, before the command, end the step with an error when the value starts with -, such as [[ $X != -* ]] || exit 1 for the variable X that holds the value. findings.detected: secrets reads the secrets without naming one
findings.consequence: GitHub sends the job every secret of the repository, including the secrets that no expression of the job names, and also every secret of the environment of the job when the job references an environment. The memory of the runner holds every secret that GitHub sends the job, and code that runs in a step of the job can read every secret in the memory of the runner. The harm comes from two kinds of code: an action that turns malicious, and code that an attacker writes and that a flaw of the job runs. The harm is each secret that one of the two kinds of code can read now and could not read if each job of each workflow that can read the secret named only the secrets that the job needs. In the workflows that name only the needed secrets, GitHub sends each job only the secrets that the job names, and code that runs in a job can still read every secret that the job names. An action counts in every job, of any workflow, that runs the action; the code of an attacker counts only in the jobs whose flaw runs the code of the attacker
findings.remedy: name each secret the job needs, secrets.NAME, and pick one by an if for each value of the matrix rather than by a secrets[...] whose name is computed

findings.detected: the job runs on a self-hosted runner (self-hosted) of a public repository

findings.remedy: run the jobs of a public repository on GitHub-hosted runners: with a label of a GitHub-hosted runner in runs-on, the rule reports nothing. An owner of the organization can instead put the self-hosted runners in a runner group that does not allow public repositories: no job of the repository reaches those runners; declare a label of runs-on that only those runners have trusted with the fact repo.runner-label-trusted (true for the label, in a file of facts, --fact, or fact in --config), and the rule reports nothing for the job (otherwise the false positive form group-access). An ephemeral runner removes the files and the processes that a job leaves on the machine of the runner before the next job, and the code of a pull request still reaches the network of the runner while the job runs.
